corrections: contract-relations-and-ending: the seat's own earlier sentence (commit b4c54fce) said Flag as confidential sets the other Contract's flag. The link dialog flags whichever side is not Confidential, which can be the current Contract. The guide now says the prompt names that Contract and that it can be this Contract or the one you linked; the walkthrough exercised both directions and the dismissal.

create-contract: the Contract type control lives on Overview, not in the Fields section the surrounding paragraph describes; the guide now says so. The C14 walkthrough for both roles ran on the corrected bytes.
Both changes were made before the final two-role runs of those guides; the author records keep the hashes they ran against.
observations: Earlier reviewer runs failed on harness assumptions, not on app or guide behaviour: the Matter search renders buttons rather than options; Amount is a number input stored in minor units; Counterparties and team sit beside, not inside, the Contract object; a stale "Saved" note read before the PATCH landed; the Team removal control is named "Take … off the team as …"; the header Stage button is named by Stage, not Status; the Status pill sits outside the main landmark; picking the current Status again sends no PATCH; the Stage menu's last item sat outside a 720 px viewport; approval rows carry avatar initials and "Requested by"; a first PATCH refused by the Soft gate answers 409 before the override; the current Version's executed action is in the Document row menu; Document Versions expose versionNumber and isExecuted; the term dates are calendar pickers with month and year dropdowns while Task and Key date dialogs use plain date inputs; the Task assignee popover is the "Assign task" dialog; Home cards list a few rows before View all; the Link type is a select; relation subsection headings render uppercase; the Filter button's accessible name carries its active count ("Filter 1"). Each was corrected in the harness and the run repeated; the final records hold only the completed runs on the final bytes.

The Contract Status menu is crowded in these disposable labs: the seeded Statuses plus fixture Statuses from earlier batches and this review give about twenty live options. At an ordinary 1280×720 viewport the menu extends below the viewport with overflow hidden and its last option cannot be clicked; a separate read-only probe recorded this and it is tracked as issue #768. The walkthroughs used 1280×1800 contexts to reach every option; that is a harness workaround, not a claim that the ordinary-height menu passed.

A Contract's current Version is marked from the Document row's Actions menu; the version-level Actions menu appears only for earlier Versions under "N earlier versions of …". The manual-signing guide's "that Document Version's actions" holds for both, so no text change was made.

The blank-subject default was confirmed through the actual send: the provider received "C-<number> <title>" for both roles. The controlled outage message reads "The provider could not be reached. It may still have taken the envelope — check at the provider before you send again."
On a Confidential Contract, naming a person without access answers 422 and applying a group with such a member is refused by name; neither asks anybody. The picker itself never offers the person.

Home lists a few assigned Tasks and approaching dates per card; the reviewer's Task and Key date were reached through View all (/home/tasks and the "Your dates" calendar dialog) when the card did not show them.
The Contracts list needed several Show more pages to reach the reviewer's Ended record after Show ended; the earlier list problem in issue #751 is not claimed fixed.
limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author; not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.

C17 electronic signing ran against the declared local DocuSign protocol stand-in with fictional Signers and generated keys; it verifies OpenLaw's workflow handling, not real provider configuration (C42), and no external signing transaction occurred.

Browser contexts were 1280×1800 CSS px so the crowded Stage menu of these disposable labs stayed reachable (issue #768); layout checks in the discovery record are CSS-pixel measurements, not browser zoom or assistive technology acceptance.

Competing writes and prerequisite records were applied through the lab APIs by the acting or second staff session; external email delivery and reminder timing were not claimed (the notifications guide owns them).

Linked guides remain unpublished: Document Versions (DOC-017), Contract analysis (DOC-015), Matter creation (DOC-016), Approver groups (DOC-021) and Signing connector setup (DOC-022); the shared access, conversation and notification guides carry their own dependencies. All eight articles stay in review.
